surprises.description: The commercial portfolio reached $15 billion, above the preview’s expected $13.6–14.0 billion range. Management also raised expected full-year growth excluding the Panama loan to around 25%, well above the original 13%–15% guidance.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The commercial portfolio reached a record $15 billion, up 15% quarter-over-quarter and 38% year-over-year”; excluding the Panama loan, full-year growth is expected around 25%, with the total including Panama around 35%.
surprises.expectation_evidence: “Commercial portfolio was $13.0B at 2Q26 against a 13–15% FY growth guide implying ~$13.1–13.3B by year-end — so the portfolio may print above guidance (~$13.6–14.0B) purely on this deal.”

surprises.description: Net interest income and quarterly NIM came in above the preview’s expected ranges: NII was $79.8 million versus about $76–78 million, and NIM was 2.30% versus about 2.20%–2.28%. The margin gain was partly supported by unusually high loan prepayments and lower funding costs, which management described as temporary benefits.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net interest income hit a record $79.8 million” and “NIM rose 6 basis points to 2.30%”; management attributed the gain partly to loan prepayments running 2–3x higher than usual and lower funding costs.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview estimated “Net interest income … ~$76–78M” and “NIM … ~2.20–2.28%.”

surprises.description: Net income was below the preview’s $66–68 million estimate at $63.2 million, despite record NII. The company attributed the sequential decline partly to normalized fee income, higher expenses, and increased provisions.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Net income reached $63.2 million,” down 5% from Q2 due to “normalized fee income, higher expenses, and increased provisions.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The derived Q3 net profit estimate was “~$66–68M.”

surprises.description: Provision expense reached $10.4 million, above the preview’s expected $6–9 million range. Management said the increase mainly reflected additional coverage on existing Stage 3 exposures and portfolio growth, rather than new credit deterioration, and expected cost of risk to remain around 20 basis points.
surprises.fact_evidence: “Provision expense increased to $10.4 million from $8.6 million,” driven mainly by added reserve coverage on existing Stage 3 exposures and portfolio growth; cost of risk is expected stable around 20 basis points.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview anticipated provisions of “~$6–9M” in its base scenario and listed provision expense versus “~$6–9M” as a key catalyst.

surprises.description: Despite the Panama loan and major portfolio growth, Tier 1 ended at 16.2%, above the preview’s base-case 15.5%–16.0% range and the 15.2% estimate if the full loan were retained with a 100% risk weight. Management said much of the incremental growth used little capital.
surprises.fact_evidence: “The Tier 1 ratio ended at 16.2% (down from 16.6%), falling less than 50 basis points despite major loan growth” because growth came largely from “low-capital-consumption investment-grade sovereign and quasi-sovereign exposures.”
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario expected “Tier 1 15.5–16.0%”; it estimated that holding the Panama loan in full could take the ratio “to ~15.2%.”

surprises.description: The full-year NIM outlook was around 2.25%, below the preview’s base-case expectation of a trim to about 2.27% and the prior 2.30% guide. Management also said the Panama transaction would temporarily dilute reported NIM in Q4 even as it added meaningfully to absolute NII.
surprises.fact_evidence: Management guided that the Panama transaction will “temporarily dilute reported NIM in Q4” while adding meaningfully to absolute NII, with full-year NIM “around 2.25%,” implying roughly 5 basis points of compression.
surprises.expectation_evidence: The preview’s base scenario anticipated that “NIM guide [would be] trimmed to ~2.27%.”
